title: ph generate document-model renamed --file to --document and reassigned the -d short flag to it
content:
The manual generator flag was renamed between v6.0.0 and v6.2.2, and the short-flag reassignment is the dangerous half.

**v6.0.0** (`packages/@powerhousedao/ph-cli/dist/cli.mjs`):

```
file:  long "file",  short "f"   — path to the file to generate from
dir:   long "dir",   short "d"   — existing document model directory to re-generate
all:   long "all",   short "a"
```

**v6.2.2-dev.45**:

```
document: long "document", short "d"  — path to a .phd or .json spec
dir:      long "dir"                  — (no short form any more)
all:      long "all",      short "a"
extract:  long "extract",  short "x"
```

So `-d` moved from `--dir` to `--document`. A v6.0-era script or muscle-memory invocation of `ph generate document-model -d document-models/todo` used to mean "re-generate this existing directory" and now means "treat this path as a spec file" — a different operation on the same argument, with no deprecation warning. Prefer the long forms in anything scripted.

Two further changes: `--document` accepts `.json` as well as `.phd` (the handler branches on the `.phd` extension and falls through to `loadDocumentModel` otherwise), and `--extract` is new — it writes a `powerhouse/document-model` spec for each existing model into `specs/document-models/` instead of generating code. The command also has the alias `doc`. Supplying none of `document`, `dir`, `all`, or `extract` is not an error; it prints `Please specify one of ...` and exits.

Manual generation is only needed for the Connect export workflow. Under `ph vetra`, codegen runs automatically from the spec documents on the Vetra drive.

_Source: @powerhousedao/ph-cli dist/cli.mjs and dist/generate-document-model-*.mjs, compared across v6.0.0 and v6.2.2-dev.45. The academy's 08-DocumentModelVersioning.md still shows the flagless `ph generate TodoList.phd` form, which is dead._
description: In v6.0.0 -f was --file and -d was --dir. In v6.2.2 the flag is --document with -d as its short form, so an old -d argument now means a different thing.
